final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a policy-bounded, conditional position based on the same record. That narrowing improves precision, but it does not satisfy the unresolved compliance predicate in the policy text: certification may proceed only if current release documentation already reflects current evaluation results and discloses material segment weaknesses, or if an approved mitigation covers them. On the available record, aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support release readiness context, but they do not by themselves establish present compliance for certification. The distinction matters here: a caveat can support `compliant_with_caveats` only when it bounds an otherwise satisfied position; here the caveat is the missing policy condition itself. The strongest supportable conclusion remains that certification is plausible only after documentation completion is evidenced, so the current claim remains suspicious rather than compliant.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation or model card has already been updated to reflect current evaluation results and explicitly disclose the Spanish-language billing weakness.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the subgroup regression.
The actor's narrowed position is conditional on a pre-launch documentation update, but that condition is itself a required policy predicate rather than a resolved caveat.
Prior approval and informal monitoring remain contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-documentation requirement.
